SNP-based deletions relative to E2 in 226 strains

Each row is a strain and each column a window along the E2 chromosomes. A SNP-based deletion is a run of at least five consecutive SNPs with a missing call in that strain, in the genome-wide SNP set (Data S3, 198,454 SNPs). The colour is the fraction of the window's SNPs that lie in such a deletion. Move the mouse over the map to read the values. Click to pin a red line and click it again to remove it; the arrow keys move a pinned line by one window. Select a chromosome to view it at full width.

0 1 fraction of the window's SNPs in a SNP-based deletion in the strain window without SNPs grey italic name: median depth below 20x (SNP calls are often missing because of low depth, not deletion)
